name.text: Grammar of Graphics: Hidden changes across two years

questiontext.text:
Researchers counted the books in school libraries across three villages in Year 1 and Year 2. The same schools were visited in both years. Explore the two boxplots to find out what changed.

The graph starts with only the boxplots. You can add individual schools, connect paired measurements, colour by village, and inspect exact values. Decide which layers you need for each investigation.

Investigations

1. How many schools gained books from Year 1 to Year 2?

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]]

2. How many schools had exactly the same number of books in both years?

[[input:ans2]] [[validation:ans2]]

3. Which village had the largest average increase in books per school?

[[input:ans3]] [[validation:ans3]]

4. How many books did the school with the largest individual increase gain?

[[input:ans4]] [[validation:ans4]]

5. What do the plots and the additional visual layers tell us about change between the two years?

[[input:ans5]] [[validation:ans5]]

generalfeedback.text:
The two boxplots have identical distributions because the Year 2 values are a rearrangement of the Year 1 values. This does not mean every school stayed the same. Paired lines show which schools gained, lost or retained books; village colours show how the changes differ across villages.

To interpret paired data, distinguish the distribution in each year from the changes within individual schools. The additional visual dimensions expose relationships the marginal boxplots cannot show.

prtincorrect.text: Incorrect answer.

truefeedback.text: Correct. These are the schools whose paired lines rise from Year 1 to Year 2.
You may have counted schools that did not gain books. Count only upward-sloping paired lines.
This is the total number of schools, not the number that gained books.
These schools have horizontal paired lines. Count the upward-sloping lines instead.
This counts schools that changed in either direction. The question asks only about gains.

falsefeedback.text: Connect the measurements and count only schools with Year 2 above Year 1.

truefeedback.text: Correct. Horizontal paired lines indicate no change.
This counts schools that gained books, not schools with no change.
This counts schools that changed in either direction. Look for horizontal lines.
Not every school stayed unchanged. Reveal the paired lines.
Some paired lines are horizontal. Colour by village or inspect the schools to find them.

falsefeedback.text: A school is unchanged only when its Year 1 and Year 2 measurements are equal.

truefeedback.text: Correct. This village has the largest average positive change, visible in its upward paired lines.
This village has the largest average decrease, not increase. Check the direction of its paired lines.
This village is comparatively stable. Compare the average vertical change, not the final height of the points.

falsefeedback.text: Colour the points by village, then compare the average upward or downward changes for each village.

truefeedback.text: Correct. You subtracted Year 1 from Year 2 for the school with the largest increase.
That is the largest Year 2 measurement. The question asks how many books were gained, so subtract the two measurements for one school.
That is the largest Year 1 measurement, not an individual change.
That is the average gain across schools in the gaining village. Find the largest gain for a single school.
The sign indicates a decrease. Find the largest positive difference instead.

falsefeedback.text: Inspect a rising line and calculate Year 2 minus Year 1. Find the largest such difference.

truefeedback.text: Correct. Similar marginal boxplots can conceal individual changes and differences among villages.
Similar boxplots do not mean the same schools kept the same number of books. Reveal and connect the paired measurements.
The paired lines have different slopes and directions. Schools did not all experience the same change.
A high Year 2 value is not the same as a large increase. Compare each school with its own Year 1 measurement.

falsefeedback.text: Compare the boxplots with the connected, village-coloured observations. Which information appears only after adding layers?
